claims.text: The baseline eutectic high-entropy alloy has a conventional dual-phase lamellar colony structure.
Internal boundaries in the baseline lamellar colony structure are prone to microcrack initiation during tensile loading.
A trace microalloying addition combined with controlled aging will trigger nanoscale precipitate formation at colony boundaries.
The resulting precipitates will be coherent.
The nanoscale coherent precipitates will form at internal colony boundaries.
Boundary nanoprecipitates will enhance interfacial cohesion.
Boundary nanoprecipitates will inhibit crack initiation.
Boundary nanoprecipitates will inhibit crack propagation.
The nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase tensile strength.
The treated alloy will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength than the unmodified baseline.
The treated alloy will have greater room-temperature elongation to failure than the unmodified baseline.
Concurrent strength and ductility improvements require a uniform, optimized nanoscale precipitate distribution.
Deviations from the required aging temperature or duration may prevent the proposed improvements.

contradictions.description: The mediator is placed at internal colony boundaries, whereas the mechanism describes reinforcement of interfaces between colonies. These may be distinct interface populations, so the operative precipitate location is internally inconsistent.
